doc.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998

chapter: Leading the Basie band and recordings
title: Music quiz: the East, North, South, Wess album
summary: He identifies the Wess and Foster record with Coker and Powell, from about 1956, on 'Sweet Georgia Brown' changes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Let me try this one on ya. This is uh—
I just know you’re going to stump me.
That was two tenor saxophones, two trombones. Frank Wess and myself, Henry Coker and Benny Powell in an album called “No Count Basie,” or Frank “East, North, South, Wess.”
Yeah but what was the date?
What was the date? Why’d you ask me that? It was around 1956 I think.
Yes it was ‘56, you are exactly right. A nice little small group, mostly Basie members. That’s great. Here’s one more for you.
That by the way was based on the harmonic structure of “Sweet Georgia Brown.”
Oh. No kidding. Just borrowing those classic structures.
